steps.body: V = l × w × h records the counting in order: l × w builds one layer, and h stacks it.
steps.narration: V = l × w × h records the counting in order: l × w builds one layer, and h stacks it.

widget.prompt: Build the l × w layer for a 6-by-4 base.
widget.successFeedback: 24 cubes in the layer — multiply by the height and the formula is complete.
widget.lowFeedback: Smaller than 24 — keep building to 6 by 4.
widget.highFeedback: Larger than 24 — a side has overshot the dimensions.
widget.factorFeedback: That area is right, but from other sides — this layer must measure 6 across and 4 deep.

predict.prompt: In V = l × w × h, what does l × w produce?
predict.reveal: Two dimensions give a flat layer; the third stacks it into a solid.

cml.actionGoal: Build one layer, then count how many layers the height stacks for g5v formula lwh.
invariants: Volume is a count of unit cubes, and a prism organises that count into identical layers: the base area counts one layer and the height counts the layers, which is why g5v formula lwh is a product rather than a sum.
misconceptions: Adding the three dimensions instead of multiplying, stopping at the base area, or adding a removed notch instead of subtracting it.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the height doubled but the base stayed the same, what would happen to the cube count?

widget.prompt: Why does V = l × w × h give the same answer as counting cubes?

options.label: Because l × w counts one layer and h repeats it
options.feedback: Correct — the formula is the counting, organised: a layer first, then the stack.

options.label: Because three numbers always multiply to a volume
options.feedback: Only lengths along three perpendicular directions do; any three numbers would not.

options.label: Because the formula was chosen by convention
options.feedback: It follows from the structure of the stack rather than from agreement.

options.label: It does not always agree with counting
options.feedback: It always agrees for a right rectangular prism, because it IS the count rearranged.

widget.prompt: Compute 7 × 8 — the base area of a 7-by-8 rectangle, in square units.

commonErrors.feedback: Adding gives the distance round part of the edge, not the number of squares covering the base.
That is the perimeter of the base; area counts the squares inside it.
